title: Radicle org
description: Contents of .radicle/org.json on the default branch of an org repository: an actor repository whose xyz.radicle.actor payload carries type: "org". One repository describes exactly one org. The repository's RID is the org's identifier; its delegates are the org's admins.

version.description: Schema version, not the org's version. Moves only when the meaning of an existing field changes; additive evolution happens through new optional fields at the same version. A consumer that does not understand this value must still recognise the file as an org declaration, but must refuse to interpret its contents rather than parse it partially or treat it as malformed.

description.description: Short summary of the org. Long form content belongs in .radicle/profile/README.md.

members.description: The org's members, each named either by their actor repository (rad:, recommended for people: device-stable, resolves to a profile, attestable) or by a bare device key (did:key:, a claim-only roster entry with no member side to assert back). Membership is a claim by whoever controls this repository and grants no access to anything.

repos.description: RIDs of the repositories associated with the org. Association is a claim and does not require the repository's consent.

did.description: The lexical form of a canonical Radicle peer identifier: did:key: followed by a 48 character base58btc value beginning z6Mk. The pattern rejects the encodings used by other standard key types, but it does not prove that the decoded multicodec is ed25519-pub; consumers must decode the value for conformance.

rid.description: A repository identifier: rad: followed by a multibase base58btc encoding (leading z) of a Git object identifier. Bounded to the SHA-1 object format, the only one Radicle defines today; a new object format will require a new bound.
